title: Man Returned From Mexico, Jailed on Capital Murder Charge in Laredo Woman's Death
excerpt: Laredo police say 21-year-old Christian Onyx Benson was picked up in Monterrey and returned to Webb County on a capital murder charge in the July death of Dora Alicia Peña, 56.
content:
A 21-year-old man accused of killing a Laredo woman in July has been returned from Mexico and jailed on a capital murder charge, Laredo police said Friday, Nov. 20.

Christian Onyx Benson was picked up Thursday evening in Monterrey, Nuevo León, and the Laredo Police Department learned of the arrest around 6:25 p.m., according to police. Investigators coordinated with Mexican officials and a U.S. Marshals Service task force to bring him back. Task force officers received him at International Bridge 1 and drove him to police headquarters. Jail records list him as booked Friday in Webb County, with bond set at $1 million.

The charge stems from the death of Dora Alicia Peña, 56. A call about an unresponsive person brought officers to a home on Broadcrest Drive at about 8:22 a.m. on July 20, and Peña was pronounced dead there. Police said the death first appeared to be natural, but a medical examiner's autopsy then turned up signs of foul play, and detectives from the Crimes Against Persons Unit interviewed several people of interest, including Benson.

According to police, Benson knew Peña and her relatives and was close to her son. Investigators concluded he went inside the residence and caused her death. Police Chief Miguel Rodriguez said Benson sexually assaulted Peña and that she died of suffocation. KGNS reported that the chief also cited evidence of a blow and said Benson acknowledged to detectives that he was responsible for her death.

Police described Peña's death as the fifth homicide recorded in Laredo this year. Benson is presumed innocent unless convicted in court.

Sources: Laredo Police Department; KGNS, Nov. 20, 2026.
